key_insight: UniPool replaces isolated per-layer expert sets with a single globally shared expert pool, showing many layers can share experts with only minimal loss in accuracy.
problem_solved: Fixes the rigid per-layer expert allocation in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that forces linear expert-parameter growth with depth and assumes every layer requires its own isolated experts.
method: Introduce a globally shared expert pool (UniPool) that all transformer layers can access instead of maintaining separate expert sets per layer.
Design routing and capacity-control mechanisms so layers dynamically select from the shared pool while preserving load balance and specialization.
Use routing probes and empirical experiments to compare shared vs. per-layer allocations and quantify accuracy vs. parameter efficiency trade-offs.
impact: Enables more parameter-efficient scaling of MoE models by decoupling expert capacity from depth, simplifying architecture design and reducing training/inference cost while maintaining near-original performance.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: traditional per-layer experts vs. UniPool shared-expert architecture

paper_title: UniPool: A Globally Shared Expert Pool for Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Minbin Huang, Han Shi, Chuanyang Zheng, Yimeng Wu, Guoxuan Chen
